newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 7.

text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Monday's Sri Lankan newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VIRAKESARI
Senior Sri Lankan ministers G.L. Peiris, C.V. Gooneratne and Kingsley Wickremaratne tell Washington businessmen to invest in Sri Lanka.
A group of 25 LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam) women suicide bombers might be in Colombo, warns Colombo police chief D.M.T.B. Dissanayake.
THINAKARAN
Landmine explosion injurs 19 soldiers at Vavunativu in Batticaloa on Saturday.
Tamil political parties in parliament ask India to urge Sri Lanka to find solution to the conflict in the north and east, to stem refugee flows to south India.
DAILY NEWS
Three senior Sri Lankan cabinet ministers tell group of U.S. businessmen in Washington that the government is enacting rules to ensure level playing field for all investors.
Colombo police chief D.M.T.B. Dissanayake warns 25 members of the LTTE women's suicide squad might have come to Colombo to create unrest in the city.
THE ISLAND
Government seeks supplementary estimates of 10.5 billion rupees to increase defence spending to approximately 50 billion rupees this year.
LANKADEEPA

The main opposition United National Party (UNP) will take up government invitation to visit recently captured Jaffna peninsula and Kilinochchi only if state censorship of military news is lifted, says Gamini Atukorala, party general secretary.
DINAMINA
Four members of a group of 28 who were held by LTTE in Kilinochchi, give themselves up to government forces soon after troops captured the town last week, high-placed police sources say.
Senior UNP MP and former foreign minister A.C.S. Hameed says his party will not shirk its responsibility in helping to find solution to the conflict in the north and east.
DIVAINA
A group of people held captive by the LTTE in Kilinochchi, seek protection of govenrment troops who captured the town last week, police sources say.
--Colombo newsroom tel 941-434319
